reading: The 3x3 input is scaled into a 3x3 grid of blocks; block (i,j) is a copy of the whole input where input cell (i,j) is non-background, else empty.
why: every output block equals the input exactly when the corresponding input cell is fg, and is all background otherwise

reading: The 6x3 input is a vertically periodic pattern; it is continued to 9 rows with the same period and colour 1 becomes 2.

slots.period: smallest vertical period of the input rows (2, 4 or 3 in training)

why: output row r equals input row (r mod period) with 1 replaced by 2, for r = 0..8

reading: The objects lying on the bottom edge are taken left to right and chained diagonally from the top-left corner: each object's top-left cell is placed on the previous object's bottom-right cell, later objects overwriting earlier ones.

slots.link: next object's top-left = previous object's bottom-right cell (overlap of one cell, later on top)

why: every object keeps its shape and colour; consecutive objects share exactly one cell (corner overlap) with the later colour shown

reading: A central 3x3 shape has small coloured fragments next to it; each fragment is part of a copy of the shape offset by 4 (size+1) in that direction, and copies of the shape in the fragment's colour are repeated every 4 cells in that direction to the border.

slots.directions: one per fragment: the step from the shape's box to the fragment (orthogonal or diagonal), length 4

why: every copy equals the central shape recoloured; each fragment lies inside the first copy in its direction; copies are spaced 4 apart until the border

reading: A lattice of identical multi-coloured tiles is corrupted by scattered noise (colour 3 cells inside and outside the tiles); the output restores every tile to the common (majority) tile and clears all noise outside the tiles.

slots.tiles: the repeated rectangular blocks (same size, laid out on a regular lattice)
slots.rest: every cell outside the tiles becomes background

why: all tiles in the output are identical and equal the cellwise majority of the input tiles; non-tile cells are 0

reading: Like a self-tile, but the copy is the colour-inverted input (fg cells become background, background cells become the fg colour); block (i,j) holds this inverted copy where input cell (i,j) is fg, else empty.

slots.extent: fg cells of the input pick which 3x3 blocks are filled
slots.unit: the input with fg and background swapped (single fg colour)

why: every output block is either all background or the inverted input, exactly when the matching input cell is fg
invariants: only the input's fg colour appears

reading: A grid of 2x2 cells separated by full lines holds a few coloured cells; every empty (0) cell lying between two cells of the same colour on one row or column is filled with that colour, separator lines stay.

new_rows.name: gap0_between
new_rows.datalog:
colr(Y, X, C) :- cell(Y, X, C), C > 0.
gap0_between(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, Z), Z = 0, colr(Y, X1, C), colr(Y, X2, C), X1 < X, X < X2.
gap0_between(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, Z), Z = 0, colr(Y1, X, C), colr(Y2, X, C), Y1 < Y, Y < Y2.

why: the separator colour is the most common (background), so cell() gives 0-cells and coloured cells; each filled 0-cell takes the colour of the equal-coloured pair it lies between; no conflicts occur

reading: A 3x3 arrangement of 3x3 panels split by 5-lines; the one panel lacking colour 8 (only 4 coloured cells) is selected and upscaled: output panel (i,j) is filled entirely with the colour of that panel's cell (i,j), separators kept.

slots.chosen: the panel with the fewest non-background cells (the one without colour 8)
slots.upscale: each cell of the chosen panel fills the whole corresponding panel of the output

why: output panel (i,j) is uniform with colour = chosen panel cell (i,j); separator lines unchanged

reading: Each small cross (centre colour c, four arm cells colour a) grows into a radius-2 star: the arms extend one more cell in colour a and the four diagonals from the centre get two cells of colour c.
why: around every cross centre the 5x5 output window is the fixed star pattern with that cross's two colours; everything else stays background

reading: Blobs of colour 1 (rectangles joined by thin bridges) each contain one seed cell of another colour; every interior cell of the blob (all 8 neighbours non-background) takes the seed's colour.

new_rows.name: interior
new_rows.datalog:
nonbg(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
edge(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, !nonbg(Y2, X2).
interior(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), !edge(Y, X).

slots.subject: interior cells of each connected non-background component (the 'interior' row)
slots.colour: the single non-1 seed colour inside the same component (not the nearest seed: nearest fails)

why: within each component, a cell changes iff all its 8 neighbours are non-background, and it becomes that component's seed colour; border cells and bridges stay 1
